about: What a lab would otherwise buy for SWELL's job (tiling an expanded gel in widefield fluorescence on a motorised stage), from UK public contract award notices read 2026-10-10 by the X-WOW AI agent (cited, not verified: no person has checked them). Government records under the Open Government Licence v3.0. tools/numbers_compare.py computes the ratios against SWELL's estimated build.

like_for_like.what: automatable epifluorescence microscopy in multiple wavelengths
two widefield microscope systems for live cell imaging
like_for_like.note: the same notice also gives £308,000 (II.1.7), and the Contracts Finder copy gives £0; V.2.4's figure is used

like_for_like.what: Motorised Widefield Fluorescent Microscope System with Computer Control

manual_floor.what: an inverted fluorescence microscope with a mechanical stage and camera (no motorised stage)
an inverted fluorescence microscope with an integrated digital camera

not_like_for_like: The commercial systems do more (several channels, commercial stages, cameras and software, installation and warranty); their prices are from 2019 to 2024 and not adjusted for inflation; SWELL's range includes VAT while most award values exclude it; SWELL's range leaves out tools, labour, shipping and the wet lab, most of its lines are estimates, and it has never been built.
